title: Validated Rollout Checkpoint Playbook and Decision Matrix
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: Provide a practical playbook and decision matrix for multi-stage feature rollouts and A/B experiments that reduces judgment friction for on-call and PM owners. The playbook defines discrete validation checkpoints (data, latency, quality, cost), minimum instrumentation, escalation thresholds, and automated rollback triggers so teams can run faster, safer rollouts across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.

Scope: Applies to model serving changes (model version swaps, routing policy changes, quantization changes) and UI/console features that affect traffic partitioning. Excludes purely internal infra refactors unless they change request routing or model behavior.

Checkpoint structure (phased validation):
- Canary(Shadow) Validation (0-1% traffic, 24-48h): verify end-to-end correctness and telemetry ingestion. Primary checks: request/response schema, error-free paths, KV cache hit baseline, basic latency percentiles.
- Small Signal Roll (1-10% traffic, 48-72h): surface early quality regressions using seeded prompt sets and synthetic load. Primary checks: output quality deltas (strict and fuzzy thresholds), 95/99 latency, token cost delta.
- Confidence Ramp (10-50% traffic, rolling windows 72h): monitor user-facing metrics and aggregated eval sets. Primary checks: user-error rate, business KPIs (engagement), latency SLA adherence, cost per 1M tokens.
- Broad Release (>50% traffic, continuous): rely on long-window trend detection and automated mitigations. Primary checks: sustained quality delta within SLA, rolling rollback automation enabled.

Metrics and thresholds (examples):
- Quality: aggregated eval score delta <= -0.02 absolute (fail), warning for -0.01 to -0.02. Use a mixed metric: weighted average of safety checks (50%), relevance (30%), formatting accuracy (20%).
- Latency: p95 increase <= +25ms (warning), +50ms (fail).
- Errors: new 5xx or stream interruptions > 0.5% of requests = fail.
- Cost: per-token unit cost increase > 15% sustained over 72h = warning.

Instrumentation requirements before any rollout:
- Dedicated dashboards: per-route p50/p95/p99, error rates, request volume, cost per token, model variant breakdown.
- Eval harness: a canonical prompt set with golden labels and automated scoring (CI-run on model candidates).
- Tracing hooks: request id propagation, backend and model duration spans.
- Canary toggles: ability to pin test cohorts and toggle routing quickly (console + API).

Decision matrix and authority:
- Author (PM or Feature Owner): owns rollout runbook, approves progression if checkpoints green.
- Eng on-call (SRE): authority to pause/roll back for operational failures (latency, infra errors).
- ML owner: authority to block for quality regressions on seeded/production prompts.
- Escalation: if a checkpoint fails, immediate pause; owner triage within 30 minutes; if unresolved in 2 hours, paging to Platform Lead.

Automated mitigations and fallback policy examples:
- Automatic scale-back: if p95 latency > threshold for 10m and request queue depth observed, scale to a lower-capacity variant and re-route 50% traffic away.
- Model fallback: if quality fail detected on eval harness, route to last known-good model variant and open incident.
- Canary grace: suppress automated user-facing feature toggles until the next green checkpoint to avoid thrash.

Runbook checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] PRs linked: feature branch, infra changes, and dashboard additions.
- [ ] Eval harness baseline and golden set pushed to repo.
- [ ] Ops playbook published and on-call notified.
- [ ] Rollout toggle and traffic partition configuration ready in console.
- [ ] Run contingency: pre-approved rollback patch and communication template.

Acceptance criteria for progression:
- All primary checks green for the full checkpoint window.
- No critical customer-facing errors reported by triage channel.
- PM sign-off documented in the rollout ticket.

Artifacts and links (examples to attach before execution):
- Design/PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/rollouts/PM-84022-playbook
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/experiments/pm-84022
- Eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood/eval-harness/tree/pm-84022

Open questions / Trade-offs:
1) Threshold sensitivity: balancing false positive rollback vs. delayed remediation. Proposed: use a two-tierized alert system (warning + actionable fail) with a 2-hour human triage window before company-wide pages.
2) Cross-region discrepancies: whether to require per-region checks before global progression. Proposed: require region-parity for p95 and error rate for major regions; allow smaller regions to remain in staggered release.
3) Cost versus quality: when cost rises but quality improves slightly, require explicit PM approval to proceed.
